spans.s:
Chāyā
(‘shadow’)
------------------------------------------
Sometimes, the Hindu mythological lore gives us very interesting stories. The story of सṁज्ञा and छाया is one such.
Saṁjñā, the daughter of Tvaṣṭṛ, had been married to सूर्य, the sun-god. Unable to bear the heat and brilliance of her husband, सṁज्ञा created her double, छाया, and left her in सूर्य’s palace and disappeared. सूर्य lived with छाया under the impression that she was सṁज्ञा herself. छाया bore him two sons and a daughter: Sāvarṇi मनु, Śanaiścara (or the planet शनि) and Tapatī (the goddess of the river Tapti, in Madhya Pradesh).
See also SAṀJÑĀ and SŪRYA.
